name: Cartograph Atlas: a server-authoritative ECS column store + GPU-driven tiled compute rasterizer
philosophy: Data-oriented to the bone, GPU-driven, and server-authoritative. Three commitments. (1) ONE source of truth per fact: the engine already stores every transform in AFGBuildableSubsystem/AFGLightweightBuildableSubsystem, so the host NEVER keeps a second copy of live geometry; it keeps only derived indices (a uniform spatial grid + a Z-band index) and a tiny per-class draw table (hundreds of entries, not millions). Nothing per-building that is a pure function of transform+class is ever stored — it is recomputed in the rasterizer. (2) Stable handles, never positional indices: a TSparseArray slot id (with a generation counter) is the building's identity everywhere — grid, Z-index, network deltas, GPU instance buffer. No reindex, no redirector, no tombstone leak, no array renumbering. Mutation is O(1)/O(log N), never O(N). (3) Cost is bounded by the VIEWPORT and the FRAME, never by factory size. The map is a fixed pyramid of 256x256 tiles over the fixed 7.5km world; only DIRTY tiles in the player's area-of-interest are re-rendered, each as an independent bounded GPU dispatch with a hard primitive ceiling per frame, so a single submission can never exceed the TDR window. VRAM is a fixed atlas ceiling independent of building count. The map image is a GPU artifact computed from a compact instance buffer via indirect/instanced draws (or a compute splat), so per-event CPU is just 'mark tile dirty + patch one instance slot'.
summary: Cartograph Atlas replaces the (Z-sorted array + positional-index quadtree + never-compacting IndexRedirector) triad with a column-store ECS keyed by stable generational handles, indexed by a uniform hash grid over the game's fixed 750000x750000 cm bounds and a coarse Z-band index, so every add/remove is O(1) slot + O(1) grid-cell and the O(N) reindex, the O(N^2) load, and the redirector leak all vanish at once. The host stores no second copy of geometry: it reads transforms straight from the engine subsystems per dirty cell and keeps only the grid, the Z-index, a per-CLASS draw table, and a GPU instance buffer; only thin dedicated-server clients (which lack the subsystems) keep a slim ~28-byte SoA record streamed from the server. Rendering is GPU-driven into a fixed pyramid of 256x256 atlas tiles over the world; build events mark the touched tiles dirty (a TBitArray), and a frame-budgeted scheduler re-renders at most K tiles/frame as independent bounded dispatches with a hard per-frame primitive ceiling, making TDR structurally impossible and VRAM a fixed ~84 MB ceiling regardless of 200k or 50M buildings. Convergence is monotonic dirty-tile draining (never cancel/restart): each event only ever ADDS to the dirty set and patches one instance slot, so a belt-drag converges continuously instead of thrashing. The server is the single authority: it computes per-tile content + a per-tile version once, persists nothing heavy (derived state is rebuilt from the engine on load), and streams only the tiles in a joining client's area-of-interest via the ReliableMessaging plugin as versioned deltas, fixing the #9 join crash by design (no per-join full synchronous serialize, no int16 overflow, no unchecked Find()). Network is delta-by-tile-version with backpressure, not reliable-multicast-per-event. The whole system is sized so a 1M-building factory costs the host ~40 MB of indices (vs ~430 MB today) and the client ~84 MB VRAM fixed (vs 256 MB), with per-event CPU dropping from O(N) rising-with-session to a flat handful of microseconds.
dataModel: ECS COLUMN STORE keyed by STABLE GENERATIONAL HANDLES. Identity = FBuildingHandle{uint32 slot, uint32 gen}. Storage is a TSparseArray-backed SoA (struct-of-arrays columns), NOT AoS: column Pos (FVector3f, 12B), column Yaw (float or packed int16, 2-4B), column ClassId (uint16 index into the per-class table, 2B), column Type (uint8), column ExtraIndex (uint32 into side-tables for splines/wires/beams). No FTransform (drop Quat+Scale: scale is per-class, full quat is never needed for a top-down yaw), no precomputed ScreenPosition/Corners/Size/Rotation, no VisualBoxCache, no per-building pointers. Per-CLASS data (icon texture, footprint size, category color, layer) lives in a TMap<uint16 classId, FClassDrawInfo> ClassDrawTable sized by distinct classes (hundreds), built once at gather. SPATIAL INDEX = uniform hash grid TMap<FIntPoint, TArray<uint32 slot>> (or a flat TArray of cells since bounds are fixed: ~15000x15000cm cells => 50x50 = 2500 fixed cells, each a small TArray) — O(1) insert/erase by stable slot, O(cells-in-radius) query, no per-element FBox2D, no redirector, no renumbering on mutation. Z-HEIGHT FILTER = separate coarse Z-band index: bucket slots into ~64 fixed Z-bands (TArray<TArray<uint32>> by band, or per-cell band bitmask); slider maps to a band range, intersected with the spatial query — decoupled from storage so the master columns never need sorting (kills the operator<=> coupling that forced the whole Z-sort). WHAT IS STORED vs RECOMPUTED vs QUERIED: stored = grid + Z-index + ClassDrawTable + GPU instance buffer + (client-only) slim SoA columns. Recomputed at draw = screen position, corners, rotation, footprint (pure fn of Pos+Yaw+ClassDrawTable, done in the vertex/compute shader). Queried from engine each dirty-cell pass (HOST ONLY) = the authoritative transforms, read by const-ref from AFGLightweightBuildableSubsystem::mBuildableClassToInstanceArray and AFGBuildableSubsystem (no by-value copy). Handle stability: generation counter invalidates stale references on slot reuse, so network deltas and UI picks never alias a recycled slot.
renderPipeline: GPU-DRIVEN TILED ATLAS, never one unbounded pass. The map is a FIXED PYRAMID over the fixed 750000x750000 cm world: a virtual 4096x4096 base resolution partitioned into a grid of 256x256 tiles (16x16 = 256 tiles), physically backed by a TILE ATLAS texture of ~4096x4096 RGBA8 (64 MB) plus a small residency cache so only on-screen tiles are physically resident; mips/LOD are a coarse 1024x1024 overview (4 MB) for the zoomed-out view, regenerated only for dirty tiles. PER-EVENT: an add/remove computes which tile(s) the building's footprint touches and sets bits in a TBitArray DirtyTiles + patches ONE slot in a persistent GPU instance buffer (StructuredBuffer of {posXY, yaw, classId, type}); no clear, no full-canvas tile, no re-walk. PER-FRAME: a budgeted scheduler pops up to K dirty tiles, and for each tile issues ONE bounded GPU pass — hardware ClearRenderTargetView scissored to that tile (free, not a rasterized opaque quad), then an INSTANCED/INDIRECT draw (DrawIndexedInstancedIndirect) of just the instances whose footprint intersects the tile, gathered via the spatial grid into a per-tile instance range. Geometry (rect corners, spline segments as a thin instanced quad strip, wire/beam as a line instance) is generated in the vertex shader from the compact instance record + ClassDrawTable (SRV), so the CPU emits a handful of indirect-draw args, not millions of FCanvas DrawItems. Icons are a texture-array/atlas sampled by classId — pre-pinned before the pass so no AsyncLoadObject ever stalls mid-draw. HARD GPU BOUND: each tile pass has a fixed instance ceiling and the scheduler caps total instances/frame (MaxPrimitivesPerFrame ~20-40k); a megabase full rebuild drains over many frames, each frame a tiny independent submission << TDR window. Replaces the global FCanvas::GetBatchedElements hook (process-wide tax) with a dedicated render target + RDG pass owned by the mod. Mod-feasibility: instanced draws + RDG compute are public RHI/RenderCore (already a dep) on UE5.3; version-gate any 5.3-specific RDG helper. Fallback path if RDG-from-mod proves fragile: keep FCanvas but emit ONE instanced-style batch per tile and EndDraw per tile (bounded submission) — still kills TDR, slightly higher CPU.
asyncThreading: Convergence is MONOTONIC ACCUMULATION, never cancel/restart. There is no redraw coroutine that gets Cancel()ed on every event. Instead: build hooks run O(1) on the game thread (patch instance slot + set dirty bits) and enqueue nothing heavy. A single persistent tile-scheduler coroutine runs every frame under a FRAME-RELATIVE budget (reuse the existing FTickTimeBudget model: a fraction of frame time, e.g. r.Cartograph.FrameBudgetFraction=0.15, NOT an absolute ms — directly answers issue #10) and drains the DirtyTiles set: it never discards completed tiles, it only ever shrinks the dirty set, so a belt-drag converges tile-by-tile and the already-rendered tiles stay valid. Off the game thread: (a) the per-dirty-cell engine-transform gather and the slim-record packing for network deltas run on a worker (UE::Tasks/async), producing the GPU instance-buffer patches and delta payloads; the game thread only applies the small mapped-buffer writes. (b) GPU work is on the render thread via RDG, fully decoupled — the game thread issues bounded indirect-draw args and returns. Backpressure: if dirty tiles accumulate faster than the budget drains (mass paste), the scheduler coalesces (a tile dirtied 100x is rendered once) and prioritizes tiles in the player's current viewport/AoI first, so the visible map converges first while off-screen tiles lazily catch up. No FCancellationGuard-protected O(N) ingestion block exists anymore because ingestion is O(1).
networkTransport: DELTA-BY-TILE-VERSION over the ReliableMessaging plugin, never reliable-multicast-per-event. The server maintains a per-tile content version (uint32, bumped when any building in that tile changes) and a per-tile compact instance blob (the slim SoA slice for that tile). LIVE UPDATES: instead of ClientUpdateBuildingData NetMulticast Reliable per build event, the server batches dirty-tile version bumps and pushes, per client, only the deltas for tiles in that client's AREA OF INTEREST (driven by the client's map viewport + World Partition streaming source), coalesced per net-tick — so a mass-build sends a handful of tile blobs, not N reliable RPCs. JOIN: the joining client requests tiles lazily for its AoI; the server replies with versioned tile blobs streamed via UReliableMessagingSubsystem::SendTaggedMessage(player, Cartograph.TileSync tag, payload) — a reliable large-payload tagged channel over EOS/Steam/TCP that exists precisely for this. This fixes #9 BY DESIGN: no per-join synchronous full-dataset Archive<<CurrentBuildingData on the game thread (replaced by lazy per-tile pull off the critical path); no int16 slice counter (the plugin owns chunking/acking with proper widths); no unchecked TMap::Find()/timeout race in a hand-rolled RCO (the plugin owns lifetime, keyed on player component, torn down on logout); no move-unsafe FBufferWriter-in-a-TMap. Backpressure + windowing are handled by the transport; we add a 1-byte protocol version + per-tile version so a reconnecting/late client only pulls tiles whose version it lacks (idempotent, resumable). Bandwidth: a tile blob is slim records (~28B each) + RLE for empty tiles; only changed tiles cross the wire.
serverClientPartitioning: Explicit split. COMPUTED ONCE AND STORED ON THE SERVER (authoritative, clients never recompute on join/chunk-load): the per-tile version table, the per-tile slim instance blobs, the ClassDrawTable, and the spatial grid + Z-index. These are derived from the engine subsystems and are rebuilt cheaply at world-load by one O(N) streaming pass over AFGBuildableSubsystem/AFGLightweightBuildableSubsystem (no O(N^2), no second copy) — NOT persisted in the save (avoid bloating the save and the IFGSaveInterface path); the derived state is a runtime cache, reconstructed deterministically from authoritative engine state on load, then kept incrementally correct by the build hooks. (Optional: cache the rendered tile atlas to a per-save sidecar on disk so reopening a world skips first-paint, invalidated by tile version — pure latency win, never a correctness dependency.) ALIGNED TO WORLD PARTITION: tiles map 1:1 onto fixed world cells, so a client only pulls tiles whose region its WP streaming sources cover — area-of-interest streaming for free; chunk-load on the client triggers a tile-version check, not a recompute. SINGLE-PLAYER / LISTEN HOST = server+client in one process: the host computes the indices and renders directly from engine transforms; there is NO slim client store and NO network path at all (zero serialization, zero duplication) — the same code with the transport stubbed. DEDICATED SERVER: server holds indices + per-tile blobs but renders NOTHING (no atlas, no RDG, no FCanvas — saves all VRAM and render-thread cost); each thin client holds ONLY the slim SoA columns for its AoI tiles (it lacks the subsystem data, so this is its sole source) and does all rendering locally from those. TRADE: server spends modest CPU (incremental tile versioning) + RAM (per-tile blobs ~ slim-record size, ~28 MB @1M) + bandwidth (only changed AoI tiles) to save every client from recomputing; clients spend GPU (their own atlas, fixed VRAM) + a slim store, never CPU on a second full dataset.
memoryModel: HOST (listen/single-player): NO geometry copy. Resident = uniform grid (2500 fixed cells, slot ids only: ~4B/live building amortized) + Z-band index (~4B/building) + ClassDrawTable (~hundreds of entries, KBs) + GPU instance buffer (~16B/building, render-side) + atlas VRAM. So host CPU-RAM is ~8-12B/building of indices vs ~430MB-equiv today. The ~152-192B/building precomputed caches and the ~344-432B FBuildingData are DELETED — geometry is read live from the engine and consumed transiently per dirty cell, never stored. DEDICATED-SERVER client: slim SoA columns only for AoI tiles (~28B/building for in-AoI, near-zero for streamed-out tiles) + its own atlas VRAM; no engine subsystem dependency. DEDICATED SERVER: per-tile slim blobs (~28B/building) + indices, NO atlas/VRAM. VRAM is a FIXED CEILING set by the atlas (64MB base 4096^2 RGBA8 + 4MB overview + ~16MB residency/scratch ~= 84MB) INDEPENDENT of building count — 200k, 1M, or 50M buildings all cost the same VRAM because the image is viewport-sized, not factory-sized. The instance StructuredBuffer (16B/building) is the only count-scaling GPU buffer and can itself be paged per-AoI. Generational handles add 4B/slot for the gen counter. Net: peak RAM and VRAM both decoupled from the runaway growth — flat across a build/dismantle session (no redirector tombstone leak, no quadtree append-only growth).

keyRisks: RDG/compute rasterization from a MOD on CSS's UE 5.3.2 fork: public RenderCore/RHI is available (already a dep) but some RDG helpers/shader-permutation registration may need a uplugin shader directory and version-gating; mitigation = ship the instanced-FCanvas-per-tile fallback (bounded EndDraw per tile) which kills TDR with zero custom shaders, then upgrade to full GPU-driven once the shader path is validated.

Reading engine transforms live per dirty-cell assumes AFGLightweightBuildableSubsystem exposes a stable, cheap per-class/per-cell iteration; if its layout forces a near-full scan per dirty region, the host must keep a thin position column (still ~12-16B/building, far below today's 344-432B) as a spatial cache rather than re-querying — quantify against the real subsystem API before deleting the host store entirely.

Generational-handle slot reuse must be coordinated with network deltas: a slot freed and reused between two delta batches could alias; the gen counter guards it but the per-tile blob must carry (slot,gen) or the client must clear-then-apply per tile version to stay idempotent.

Spline/belt footprints can span many tiles (a long conveyor); a single edit may dirty a strip of tiles. Mitigated by treating long splines as per-segment instances bucketed into their own tiles, but worst-case a trans-map belt dirties O(sqrt(tiles)) tiles — still bounded and budget-drained, not O(N).

World Partition AoI alignment assumes the map UI's view region and the WP streaming sources can be reconciled; if a player opens the full map zoomed out, AoI = whole world and the client must stream all tiles — handled by the coarse 1024^2 overview (4 MB, always resident) so zoomed-out is cheap and full-detail tiles stream on zoom-in.

Determinism of the runtime-rebuilt derived cache vs the authoritative save: if Cartograph derived state is NOT persisted, world-load must deterministically reproduce identical tile versions, else a reconnecting client's cached versions mismatch; mitigation = version = hash of authoritative content, not a session-local counter.
killerFeature: Cost is bounded by the VIEWPORT and the FRAME, not by the factory. The map image is a fixed-size GPU artifact (84 MB VRAM ceiling, K dirty 256x256 tiles per frame, each a bounded indirect-draw submission) that is identical whether the world holds 200k or 50M buildings — so TDR is structurally impossible, VRAM never grows, and per-event CPU collapses to O(1) 'patch one stable-handle slot + set a dirty bit', simultaneously dissolving the O(N) reindex, the O(N^2) load, the redirector leak, the second-copy RAM, the unbounded GPU pass, and (via lazy versioned per-tile streaming over ReliableMessaging) the dedicated-server join crash — all as consequences of one decision: stop storing/redrawing the whole factory, and instead index it by stable handle and render it by dirty tile.

name: Atlas — Server-Authoritative Tiled Streaming Map Pyramid
philosophy: Treat the factory map exactly like a slippy web map (Google Maps / OSM tile server). The world is a fixed quadtree of fixed-pixel tiles with an LOD/mip pyramid. The SERVER is the single tile authority: it owns the spatial index, bakes tiles, versions them, and streams baked tiles (or, for vector clients, per-tile building lists) on demand aligned to the client's area-of-interest. A tile is the universal unit of work, of cache, of invalidation, of network transfer, and of GPU cost. Nothing is ever recomputed globally; only DIRTY tiles re-bake, and only VISIBLE tiles composite. Every per-event cost is O(tiles touched) (a small constant), never O(N). VRAM, RAM, GPU-per-frame and bandwidth are all bounded by the viewport, never by factory size. The second copy of the factory and the index-redirector are deleted outright: identity is a stable handle, spatial queries are a bucketed grid, and the height filter is a separate Z-index — the three roles that the old Z-sorted-array+positional-quadtree+redirector triad fatally conflated are fully decoupled.
summary: Atlas replaces Cartograph's three conflated roles (storage / spatial culling / Z-filter, glued together by a positional-index quadtree and a never-compacting redirector) with a stable-handle SoA store, a fixed uniform hash grid keyed by stable id, and a separate Z-band index — collapsing every add/remove from O(N) (O(cumulative-lifetime-adds) in practice) to O(1) amortized and the initial load from O(N^2) to O(N). The render target stops being one fixed 8192^2 (256 MB) surface rasterized in a single unbounded GPU pass; instead the world is a quadtree of 256^2 tiles with an LOD/mip pyramid, only dirty tiles re-bake (each its own bounded GPU pass, hardware-cleared, capped at K tiles/frame), and the visible UI composites a handful of resident tiles — making TDR structurally impossible and pinning VRAM to a fixed pool (~80 MB) independent of factory size. Convergence switches from cancel/restart-on-every-event to a monotone dirty-tile set drained under a frame-relative budget (issue #10), so work is never thrown away mid-drag. The server bakes/owns tiles once and streams baked PNG-like tile blobs (rendered clients) or per-tile slim building lists (dedicated thin clients) over the existing ReliableMessaging bulk channel with per-tile versioning and delta invalidation — fixing #9 by deleting the entire hand-rolled slice RCO (null-deref, int16 overflow, move-unsafe FBufferWriter, per-join full serialize) and replacing per-event reliable multicast with coalesced per-tile version-bump deltas. On a listen host the server reads engine subsystems directly and keeps zero second copy; on a dedicated server it keeps a slim authoritative store; thin clients hold only the tiles in their area of interest. Derived tiles are cached to disk and embedded in the save via IFGSaveInterface so a re-join or chunk-load never recomputes. Net: 1M-building client RAM drops from ~360-430 MB to ~24 MB resident (viewport-bounded), VRAM from 256 MB to ~80 MB, join from an O(N) synchronous serialize + thousands of ping-pong RTTs to a lazy O(viewport) tile pull, and per-event cost from seconds to microseconds.
dataModel:
DELETE the triad: TArray<FBuildingData> CurrentBuildingData (Z-sorted), TQuadTree<int32>, and BuildingDataIndexRedirector all go.

STORE (authoritative, SoA, structure-of-arrays for cache-friendly bakes): a slot-stable container indexed by a generational handle FBuildingId{uint32 index; uint32 gen}. Backed by parallel TArrays (free-list for slot reuse): uint32 ClassHash[]; FVector3f Pos[] (single-precision world cm; ~0.05 cm worst-case error at the 7.5 km edge, visually irrelevant); uint16 Yaw[] (quantized 0..65535); uint8 Type[] (Icon/Rectangle/Spline/Wire/Beam); uint32 ExtraIndex[] (side-table index for splines/wires/beams, INDEX_NONE otherwise). Scale and quaternion are NOT stored (the wire format already proves they are droppable). Per-record resident cost ~22 B SoA-packed (vs 344-432 B FBuildingData) = 15-20x shrink. Spline/wire/beam side-tables hold the few thousand polyline records out-of-line, so a belt pays for its 9-point polyline only if it is one. NOTHING derived is stored: ScreenPosition, Size, Corners[4], Rotation, VisualBoxCache are all recomputed by a pure ComputeDrawGeometry(record, classInfo) at BAKE time only, and only for buildings in a dirty tile.

PER-CLASS TABLE (sized by classes ~ hundreds, not buildings): TMap<uint32, FClassDrawInfo> built once at gather — icon texture, world size, category/layer, extra-rotation. The four per-record pointers the old design stored per-building (CategoryData, LayerData, SplineData, WireData) become one hash lookup per class at bake.

SPATIAL INDEX: a fixed uniform hash grid over the known compile-time bounds (750000x750000 cm). Cell == one finest-LOD tile footprint (~2929 cm for a 256-tile grid, or tune to building+clearance). TMap<FIntPoint, TArray<FBuildingId>> (or a flat 2D cell array since bounds are fixed). Insert/remove = O(1) push/swap-remove of a stable id into the overlapped cell(s); region query visits only overlapping cells. No node splitting, no payload-remap, no redirector, no tombstones.

Z-INDEX (height filter, decoupled): coarse 1 m Z-bands TMap<int32, TBitArray> or a sorted TArray<TPair<float,FBuildingId>> updated O(log N) per mutation. The height slider selects a band range and the bake intersects it per-tile; it never touches storage ordering, so positions stay stable and the slider taxes only re-baked tiles, not every build event.

WHAT IS STORED vs RECOMPUTED vs QUERIED-FROM-ENGINE: On the LISTEN HOST the STORE is optional — the host can iterate AFGBuildableSubsystem / AFGLightweightBuildableSubsystem per dirty cell and keep ONLY the grid + Z-index of stable ids (zero second copy). On a DEDICATED SERVER and on CLIENTS the slim SoA store is the source of truth (clients receive it per-tile via the network). Derived geometry is always recomputed at bake; tiles (the baked pixels) are the cache.

COMPLEXITY: initial load O(N) (single pass: push into grid + Z-band + mark covering tiles dirty — the provably-never-taken redirector reindex is gone); single placement O(1) amortized (one grid push, one Z-band insert, mark <=4 tiles dirty); drag of K O(K); mass-dismantle of K O(K) (swap-remove from grid cell, free slot — no array memmove, no equal-Z linear scan, no redirector walk); region query O(cells overlapping the region).
renderPipeline:
Map = a quadtree/mip PYRAMID of fixed 256x256 RGBA8 tiles over the 7.5 km world.

PYRAMID GEOMETRY: LOD0 (finest) = a 32x32 grid of 256^2 tiles == an 8192^2 logical surface at the SAME ~1.1 cm/px the current monolith gives, but never materialized as one texture. LOD1..LOD5 each halve resolution (16x16, 8x8, ... 1x1), built by box-downsampling 4 parent tiles -> 1 child (the cheap mip step), so zoomed-out views composite few coarse tiles and zoomed-in views composite few fine tiles. A tile is baked into a small transient scratch render target (one 256^2 or a 1024^2 atlas slab holding 16 tiles) then COPYRESOLVED into a persistent tile-pool texture/atlas; the scratch is reused, so peak VRAM is the pool + one scratch slab, not the whole map.

BAKE (per dirty tile, off the single-pass trap): for each dirty tile, BeginDrawCanvasToRenderTarget on the 256^2 scratch -> hardware ClearRenderTargetView of just that tile (NOT a full-screen opaque FCanvasTileItem; the old 67 M-texel clear becomes a 65 k-texel HW clear) -> query the grid for the tile's cells -> for each building intersect Z-band filter -> ComputeDrawGeometry -> emit its icon/rect/spline/wire/beam DrawItems -> EndDraw (one bounded RHI submission per tile) -> resolve into the pool -> propagate dirty up the mip chain (re-box-downsample the 4-parent->1-child path, also bounded). Because each tile is its own EndDraw, a megabase full rebuild becomes ceil(dirtyTiles / tilesPerFrame) bounded submissions across many frames — NO single submission ever rasterizes the whole factory, so the Windows ~2 s TDR is structurally unreachable.

HARD GPU BOUND: a config MaxTilesPerFrame (e.g. 8 tiles == 8 bounded ~65 k-texel passes) caps GPU work per frame regardless of factory size or how many tiles are dirty; the remainder stays queued in the dirty set and drains over subsequent frames (self-healing, monotone).

COMPOSITE (UI): the map widget samples only the LOD and the handful of pool tiles overlapping the current viewport (typically 4-12 tiles) via a Slate brush / material reading the tile atlas — zero recompute on pan/zoom, just texture sampling. Texture icons are pre-resolved and pinned before any bake loop so no AsyncLoadObject ever stalls mid-pass.

KILL THE GLOBAL HOOK: drop the process-wide SUBSCRIBE(FCanvas::GetBatchedElements) that reroutes every game canvas. Scissoring is now intrinsic (each bake targets exactly one 256^2 tile), so unrelated HUD/UMG canvases keep the stock fast path with zero mod allocation/dispatch.

VRAM CEILING (factory-independent): tile pool of ~512 resident tiles (covers viewport + generous prefetch ring across LODs) at 256^2 RGBA8 = 256 KB/tile -> ~128 MB cap, tunable down to ~64 MB; plus one 1024^2 scratch slab (4 MB). Practical fixed budget ~80 MB, vs the old permanent 256 MB.
asyncThreading:
CONVERGENCE MODEL (no cancel/restart thrash): replace RedrawMap's Cancel()+restart with a single long-lived baker coroutine that owns a monotone DirtyTiles set (TSet<FTileId> per LOD, or a TBitArray over the fixed tile count). Build/remove events NEVER cancel in-flight work and NEVER touch the canvas — they only (a) mutate the grid/Z-index/store (O(1)) and (b) OR the covering tile ids into DirtyTiles. Completed tile bakes are committed to the pool and are never thrown away; a tile re-dirtied mid-bake is simply re-queued. There is no per-event coroutine churn and no re-paid O(N) ingestion block.

FRAME-RELATIVE BUDGET (issue #10 verbatim): keep the existing FTickTimeBudget (it already correctly yields by fraction-of-frame wall time, not absolute ms) but yield ONCE PER TILE (or per small batch of buildings within a tile), not once per primitive/edge/segment as today — eliminating the millions of per-primitive await_ready / FPlatformTime::Cycles() reads on a large rebuild. Per frame the baker pops up to MaxTilesPerFrame from DirtyTiles, bakes them while under budget, yields, resumes next tick. The budget bounds GAME-thread emission AND, because each tile is a separate EndDraw, the GPU submission per frame is bounded too (the old design's fatal gap: budget paced only the emitter while the GPU got one giant pass).

OFF THE GAME THREAD: (1) Tile encoding/compression for network (RGBA8 -> RLE/PNG-like or BC-style block compress) runs on a worker (UE5Coro async / TaskGraph), never on the game thread. (2) On the host, gathering engine buildables for a dirty cell and running ComputeDrawGeometry (pure math + per-class hash lookups) is parallelizable per tile across worker threads, with only the final BeginDraw/Emit/EndDraw marshalled to the render thread. (3) The server's per-tile serialize for the network is computed once per version on a worker and cached. (4) Mip-downsample of parent->child tiles is a GPU copy pass, off the game thread entirely. The only strictly game-thread work is the O(1) store/grid/Z mutation in the build hooks and the marshalling of bounded bake passes.
networkTransport:
DELETE the hand-rolled slice RCO entirely (CartographRemoteCallObject): that is where #9 lives — the three unchecked *TMap::Find() null-derefs on the timeout/rejoin race, the int16 slice-count overflow at ~63 MB, the move-unsafe FBufferWriter-by-value in a TMap, the fixed-2047-byte stack-tail leak, and the per-join synchronous Archive << CurrentBuildingData. None of it survives.

TRANSPORT = the in-repo ReliableMessaging plugin's bulk channel: SendTaggedMessage(Player, FGameplayTag, TArray<uint8>) + RegisterTaggedMessageHandler(Tag, FOnBulkDataReplicationPayloadReceived) (delegate signature (FGameplayTag, TArray<uint8>&&), with built-in inbound queuing for late handlers). It is purpose-built reliable large-payload messaging with correct move semantics and backpressure — it replaces every byte of the slice protocol, so the null-deref/overflow/double-free class of bug cannot exist by construction.

JOIN (lazy, area-of-interest, fixes #9 by design): on join the client sends its initial viewport/AOI; the server replies with ONLY the baked tiles (or per-tile slim building lists for thin vector clients) overlapping that AOI at the appropriate LODs — a few hundred KB, not the whole factory. As the player pans/zooms or World-Partition chunks stream in, the client requests additional tiles by id; the server answers from its per-tile version cache (already serialized once). No global serialize, no thousands of ping-pong RTTs, no fixed timeout race.

DELTA UPDATES (replace reliable-multicast-per-event): build/remove events bump the version of the affected tile(s) server-side. The server coalesces version bumps over a short window (e.g. 0.5-1 s) and sends each client a small "these tile ids changed to version V" notice (unreliable/sequenced is fine — a dropped notice self-heals on the next snapshot or when the client next samples the tile). The client re-requests only the dirtied tiles it currently holds in its AOI; tiles outside the AOI are simply marked stale and re-pulled if the player navigates there. This makes mass-build/dismantle cost O(changed tiles), not O(events x clients) of reliable FBuildingData arrays.

BACKPRESSURE & VERSIONING: ReliableMessaging provides ordered reliable delivery and queues; the protocol adds a 1-byte version header and per-tile uint32 version so a client can de-dup, request-coalesce, and detect staleness. A slow client simply pulls tiles slower; it never overflows a reliable channel with per-event multicasts.
serverClientPartitioning:
COMPUTED-ONCE-AND-STORED ON THE SERVER (clients never recompute on join or chunk-load): the authoritative spatial grid + Z-index + slim SoA store, the BAKED TILE PYRAMID (pixels), and the per-tile serialized network blobs + per-tile uint32 versions. The server bakes each tile exactly once per version; every client that ever needs that tile receives the identical cached blob. Joining or streaming a new World-Partition chunk = pulling already-baked tiles, never re-rasterizing.

LAZY / AOI-ALIGNED DELIVERY: the client pulls only tiles overlapping its current map viewport (and a prefetch ring), at the LOD it is zoomed to, aligned to World-Partition chunk streaming — when WP streams a region in, the client may request that region's coarse tiles; it never holds the whole map. Per-tile versioning + delta invalidation means a changed tile bumps its version and only clients holding that tile in AOI re-pull it.

PERSISTENCE: baked tiles + versions are cached to disk (per-save derived-data cache) and the most-relevant coarse LODs are embedded in the save via IFGSaveInterface, so a reload or a re-join skips the cold bake entirely; cold-start bake of an unseen save is the only O(N) event and it is tile-budgeted across frames (never a hang).

SINGLE-PLAYER / LISTEN HOST (server+client in one process): the host IS the tile authority and reads AFGBuildableSubsystem / AFGLightweightBuildableSubsystem directly per dirty cell, so it keeps ZERO second copy of the factory — only the grid + Z-index of stable ids + the resident tile pool for its own viewport. Baking and compositing happen in-process with no network hop.

DEDICATED SERVER + THIN CLIENT: the dedicated server lacks a renderer but still owns the grid/Z/store and bakes tiles headlessly into render targets (or, for a pure data path, serves per-tile slim building lists and lets each client bake locally — chosen by config to trade server GPU/bandwidth vs client GPU). The thin client holds only its AOI tiles. The dedicated server keeps the slim SoA store (it cannot read the host subsystems on behalf of clients' needs cheaply, so it is authoritative); the client never reconstructs global state.

EXPLICIT TRADE: server spends CPU/RAM/disk to bake-and-cache tiles ONCE (RAM ~ tile pool + slim store; disk ~ cached pyramid) so that every client spends near-zero CPU/GPU/RAM on join and on navigation. Bandwidth is AOI-bounded (a few hundred KB on join, KB-scale deltas) instead of one O(N) blob per joiner. This deliberately moves cost from the many (clients, repeatedly) to the one (server, once per version).
memoryModel:
CLIENT RESIDENT (viewport-bounded, factory-INDEPENDENT): tile pool ~80-128 MB VRAM (fixed) + the slim SoA records ONLY for buildings inside currently-held AOI tiles. At 200k or 1M buildings the client's resident RAM is dominated by the AOI working set, not the whole factory: ~22 B/record x (buildings in ~512 held tiles) ~= a few hundred-thousand records worst case at full zoom-in over the densest region, ~ single-digit to low-tens of MB. CPU/GPU per frame = composite a dozen tiles (texture samples) + drain <=8 dirty bakes.

SERVER RESIDENT: slim SoA store ~22 B/building (1M -> ~22 MB, 200k -> ~4.4 MB) + spline/wire side-tables (a few MB) + grid (TArray<FBuildingId> buckets, ~4 B/building live, no tombstones -> ~4 MB @1M) + Z-index (~few MB) + tile pool/scratch for headless bake (~80-128 MB) + per-tile cached blobs (lazy, only baked tiles; bounded by cache eviction). On a LISTEN HOST the store is dropped (engine subsystems are the source), so host adds only grid+Zindex (~10 MB @1M) + tile pool.

NO LEAKS: the redirector is deleted (the O(cumulative-lifetime-adds) scan-length growth and 4 B/lifetime-placement tombstone leak are gone); the grid uses swap-remove + free-list so it tracks LIVE count, never lifetime; tile pool is a fixed-size LRU. Resident memory is FLAT across a build/dismantle session (the #14 repro), which is the explicit success criterion.

BANDWIDTH: join ~ a few hundred KB (AOI tiles) vs old O(N) full serialize (3-18 MB) x thousands of RTTs; steady-state ~ KB-scale coalesced per-tile version deltas vs old reliable FBuildingData multicast flood per event.

complexityTable.after: O(N) — single pass: push id into grid + Z-band + OR covering tiles into dirty set; engine map iterated by const-ref; bake is tile-budgeted across frames (never a synchronous hang)

complexityTable.before: O(N) — Algo::LowerBound O(log N) + CurrentBuildingData.Insert O(N) memmove + full redirector reindex O(cumulative-lifetime-adds); cancels in-flight redraw
complexityTable.after: O(1) amortized — one grid-cell push, one Z-band insert, mark <=4 tiles dirty; no canvas cancel

complexityTable.before: O(K*N) plus permanent cancel->restart loop producing ZERO completed frames until the drag ends; RedrawArea union balloons to the whole drag
complexityTable.after: O(K) mutation; dirty tiles coalesce; baker converges continuously under frame budget, work never discarded

complexityTable.before: O(K*N) — 3 stacked O(N) ops per remove: equal-Z linear FBuildingData== scan + full redirector walk + RemoveAt tail-shift
complexityTable.after: O(K) — swap-remove stable id from grid cell, free slot, mark covering tiles dirty; no scan, no memmove, no redirector

complexityTable.before: single union AABB -> one full-screen 67 M-texel opaque clear + rasterize everything in the span in ONE unbounded GPU pass (>2 s TDR risk); auto-mip pass over full 8192^2 every redraw
complexityTable.after: O(dirty tiles) bounded passes, each a 65 k-texel HW clear + per-tile EndDraw, <=MaxTilesPerFrame/frame; mips re-derived only for the 4-parent->child path of changed tiles

complexityTable.before: O(N) synchronous Archive<<CurrentBuildingData per joiner (geometric realloc 2-3x peak) + thousands of fixed-2047-byte reliable ping-pong RTTs; int16 slice overflow >~63 MB -> never completes; null-deref on timeout/rejoin race crashes the server
complexityTable.after: O(AOI tiles) — client pulls only viewport tiles from the server's pre-baked, pre-serialized, version-cached pool over ReliableMessaging; no global serialize, no slice counter, no Find() race

complexityTable.after: O(tiles whose Z-band membership crosses the threshold) — re-bake only affected tiles; debounced; composite is just resampling

memoryEstimate.client200k: Before: ~72 MB second-copy (FBuildingData) + 256 MB VRAM = ~328 MB. After: AOI-bounded — low-single-digit to ~10 MB resident slim records + composite; full factory never resident.
memoryEstimate.client1M: Before: ~360-430 MB second-copy (RAM) + 256 MB VRAM. After: ~10-24 MB resident (AOI working set of slim ~22 B records held in viewport tiles); factory-size-independent.
memoryEstimate.server1M: Before: ~360-430 MB CurrentBuildingData + per-joiner full serialize copies (~3-18 MB each, stacking) + never-compacting redirector/quadtree growth. After: ~22 MB slim SoA store + ~4 MB grid + few MB Z-index + side-tables + ~80-128 MB headless tile pool + lazy per-tile blob cache (evictable). Listen host drops the store: ~10 MB index + tile pool.
memoryEstimate.vram: Before: fixed 256 MB (8192^2 RGBA8), permanent, + ~89 MB if auto-mips, regardless of factory size. After: fixed ~80-128 MB tile pool + 4 MB scratch slab, viewport/factory-INDEPENDENT, hard-bounded — TDR impossible because no single pass exceeds one 256^2 tile.

keyRisks: UE 5.3.2 CSS-fork API surface for per-tile baking: confirm BeginDrawCanvasToRenderTarget into a small transient/atlas RT and a true ClearRenderTargetView under scissor are reachable from a mod without engine source; if the canvas path implicitly clears or forbids sub-tile targets, fall back to a per-tile scratch RT + CopyTexture into the pool (verified mod-safe pattern). Version-gate any RDG/RHI calls.

Tile/atlas management complexity: an LRU tile pool, per-LOD dirty propagation, and AOI prefetch are real systems-engineering surface area — far more code than the current monolith. Mitigate by shipping LOD0-only first (flat 32x32 tile grid, no mip pyramid) to capture the TDR + bounded-VRAM + O(1)-mutation wins, then layer the pyramid for zoom.

ReliableMessaging assumptions: confirm SendTaggedMessage handles multi-MB payloads with the backpressure/ordering Atlas relies on, that handlers registered before connection are honored (the InboundMessagesWaitingForHandler map suggests yes), and that EOS/Steam/TCP transport variants all carry the bulk path on the live CSS network mode.

Single-precision FVector3f position (~0.05 cm error at the 7.5 km edge) and quantized yaw must reproduce the existing FillInCache geometry pixel-closely; extract one shared pure ComputeDrawGeometry helper, validate against a large save before deleting stored caches, and remove any exact-equality position compares.

Stable-handle generation semantics: if the network protocol or UI ever keys on FBuildingId across a remove+add, slot reuse needs the generation counter checked; document that tile-version is the cross-process invalidation key, not the building id.

Save-embedded derived tiles (IFGSaveInterface) risk bloating the save and going stale vs a hand-edited/older save; treat embedded tiles as a cache with a content hash, and always be able to cold-bake (tile-budgeted) if the cache misses or mismatches the live factory.

Dedicated-server headless bake needs a GPU/render context; if a truly headless server cannot bake pixels, ship the per-tile slim-building-list data path (client bakes locally) as the dedicated-server default and reserve server-side pixel baking for listen hosts.
killerFeature: VRAM, client RAM, GPU-per-frame, join bandwidth, and per-event CPU are ALL bounded by the viewport and the dirty-tile budget — never by factory size. A 1M-building megabase costs a client the same fixed ~80 MB VRAM and a dozen-tile composite as a starter base, because the tile is the universal unit of cache, invalidation, network transfer, and GPU work: only dirty tiles re-bake (each its own bounded HW-cleared pass, so the Windows TDR is structurally unreachable), only AOI tiles stream (server bakes once per version, every client pulls the same cached blob, so join is O(viewport) not O(N)), and the second-copy + index-redirector that made every build event O(N) and leaked all session are deleted outright.

name: Cartograph Atlas — Server-Authoritative Tiled Map Streaming
philosophy: Server-authoritative thin client. There is exactly ONE canonical representation of the map and it lives on the server (= the listen host in single-player, = the dedicated server otherwise): a stable-handle building store, a uniform spatial grid keyed by stable ID, a Z-band index, and a per-tile "tile snapshot" cache (one compact, immutable, versioned blob per ~250 m world tile). The client is a near-stateless consumer: it never rebuilds datasets, never reads AFGBuildableSubsystem to construct the map, and never recomputes draw geometry from the whole factory. It pulls only the tiles overlapping its current map area-of-interest (AoI), keyed by tile version; on a build event it receives a small per-tile delta (or just a "tile vX dirty" notice and re-pulls that one tile). Every cost is bounded by a constant times the WORK (tiles touched, buildings in AoI) and never by N (factory size). No structure is ever positional-index-based, nothing is ever cancel-restarted, and no GPU submission is ever unbounded. Compute moves to where it is cheapest and is done ONCE: the server computes tile snapshots once per mutation; the GPU rasterizes tiles incrementally under a hard per-frame primitive budget. We trade a modest amount of server RAM/disk (the tile cache, persisted in the save) to make join O(AoI) and chunk-load O(1) lookups instead of O(N) recompute.
summary: Cartograph "Atlas" replaces the Z-sorted array + positional-index quadtree + never-compacting IndexRedirector with a server-authoritative tiled pipeline. (1) Buildings live in a TSparseArray slot store (slot = stable BuildingId, never renumbered); spatial queries use a uniform hash grid (TMap<FIntPoint,TArray<BuildingId>>) over the fixed constexpr world bounds; the Z-height filter is served by a separate sorted Z-band index — killing the O(N) reindex, the O(N²) load, and the session-long leak at once. (2) The host never keeps a second factory copy: it iterates the engine's AFGBuildableSubsystem / AFGLightweightBuildableSubsystem per dirty tile and stores only a ~28-byte slim record plus per-class draw tables; thin clients on a dedicated server keep only the slim records for tiles in their AoI. (3) The map is a tile pyramid: the world is partitioned into a fixed grid of 256 m tiles, each backed by a small 512² render-target page in a shared atlas with a hard VRAM ceiling; redraw is a convergent dirty-tile queue that draws at most MaxPrimitivesPerFrame and flushes per frame, so no single GPU submission can hit the 2 s TDR. (4) The transport is the in-repo ReliableMessaging bulk channel: the server builds an immutable, versioned per-tile snapshot ONCE per mutation and streams the snapshots for the client's AoI; build events become per-tile deltas/version bumps, not reliable-multicast-per-event. (5) Server/client partition is explicit: the server computes and persists (via IFGSaveInterface) the tile snapshots + grid + Z-index once; the client pulls only its AoI tiles and never recomputes on join or chunk-load. (6) Memory is bounded: client VRAM is a fixed atlas budget (e.g. 96 MB) independent of factory size, and client RAM is O(AoI tiles), not O(N).
dataModel:
Three decoupled structures replace the conflated Z-sorted-array/index-quadtree/redirector triad, each serving exactly one role.

STORAGE (stable handles): `TSparseArray<FSlimBuildingRecord> Buildings`. The sparse-array slot index IS the stable BuildingId (u32; add a u16 generation counter -> 48-bit handle if any consumer keys across remove+add). Add = `Buildings.Add(rec)` -> O(1) amortized; Remove = `Buildings.RemoveAt(id)` -> O(1); positions NEVER shift, so nothing downstream is renumbered. The IndexRedirector is DELETED. `FSlimBuildingRecord` (SoA-friendly, ~28 B): { u32 classHash; FVector3f pos (12 B, single-precision is fine — 0.05 cm worst-case error at the 7.5 km edge); float16 yaw (2 B); u8 type; u32 extraIndex }. Splines/wires/beams put their polyline/endpoint payload in type-specific side-arrays indexed by extraIndex (so a belt does not pay for a rectangle cache). All precomputed draw caches (ScreenPosition, Size, Rotation, Corners[4], VisualBoxCache, FNormalDataCache/FRectangleDataCache) are DELETED from the record and recomputed by a pure `ComputeDrawGeometry(rec, classInfo)` only when a tile is rasterized. Per-class data (color, outline, size override, category, icon) lives ONCE in `TMap<u32,FClassDrawInfo> ClassDrawTable` (sized by classes ~hundreds), not per building.

SPATIAL (uniform hash grid keyed by stable ID): `TMap<FIntPoint,TArray<BuildingId>> Grid` over the fixed constexpr bounds (WEST/EAST/NORTH/SOUTH in the header), cell size ≈ tile size (256 m). Insert = hash pos -> push id: O(1). Remove = hash pos -> swap-remove id from that cell's small array: O(1) (identity is the handle, so NO equal-Z linear == scan, NO redirector walk). Region query = iterate cells overlapping the AABB: O(cells + hits). This replaces TQuadTree<int32> entirely; there is no payload-update problem because the grid stores stable IDs.

Z-HEIGHT FILTER (decoupled): `TArray<TPair<float,BuildingId>> ZIndex` kept sorted, OR coarse 1 m Z-bands `TMap<int32,TArray<BuildingId>>`. The slider does Algo::LowerBound/UpperBound (O(log N)) or band-range; the Z-filter no longer taxes every build event because STORAGE no longer needs to be Z-sorted (the `operator<=>` coupling is gone). Draw order within a tile is resolved by sorting only the tile's (few) members by Z at rasterization time.

WHAT IS STORED vs RECOMPUTED vs QUERIED-FROM-ENGINE: Stored (server, authoritative, persisted): slim records, grid, Z-index, per-tile snapshot blobs + versions, ClassDrawTable. Recomputed on demand: all draw geometry (corners/screen-pos), tile bitmaps. Queried from engine: on the host, the live transforms come from AFGBuildableSubsystem/AFGLightweightBuildableSubsystem per dirty tile, so the host can hold ONLY grid+Z-index+snapshots and skip even the slim store if desired; thin clients hold slim records only for AoI tiles.
renderPipeline:
A tile pyramid with a hard-bounded, convergent rasterizer; the single unbounded FCanvas pass and the 256 MB monolith are both eliminated.

TILING: the fixed world (≈750 km² footprint per the constexpr bounds) is partitioned into a grid of 256 m tiles (~ a 32×32 = 1024-tile grid at the base level; tile count is constant, independent of factory size). Each populated tile is rasterized into a 512² RGBA8 page (1 MB) allocated from a SHARED ATLAS texture (a fixed pool of pages, e.g. a 4096×4096 atlas = 64 pages = 64 MB, plus a small mip/overflow reserve). Empty tiles consume ZERO VRAM (no page bound). This gives a HARD VRAM CEILING independent of N: the atlas is a fixed budget; if more tiles are visible than pages, least-recently-viewed pages are evicted (the snapshot to regenerate them is cheap and server-cached).

INCREMENTAL UPDATE: a `TBitArray DirtyTiles` marks tiles whose snapshot version changed. A persistent `TileDrawQueue` drains dirty tiles. Per frame the rasterizer pops tiles and, for each, scissor-clears ONLY that tile's page (a true RHIClearRenderTargetView under scissor — not the 67 M-texel full-screen opaque FCanvasTileItem) and redraws the tile's buildings (looked up via Grid). The full-screen clear is deleted. A localized single-belt edit dirties 1–4 tiles and touches a few hundred pixels, never the whole atlas.

HARD GPU BOUND (kills TDR by construction): the draw loop counts emitted primitives; after `MaxPrimitivesPerFrame` (config, ~20 k) it calls EndDrawCanvasToRenderTarget, yields one tick (co_await NextTick), then re-Begins the SAME persistent atlas WITHOUT re-clearing and continues. One megabase full rebuild (~0.5–1 M primitives) thus becomes ceil(prims / budget) bounded RHI submissions spread over many frames — no single submission can approach the 2 s TDR threshold. Budget is frame-relative (fraction of frame time), not absolute ms (issue #10): the existing FTickTimeBudget model is kept but awaited ONCE per tile (or per K buildings), not per primitive, removing the per-primitive Cycles() overhead.

LOD / MIP PYRAMID: when zoomed out, tiles are composited at lower mip from the atlas pages; far LOD draws per-class density splats / icon-only instead of full geometry, so zoomed-out cost is O(visible tiles) not O(buildings). Mips are generated per-page lazily and only when the map UI is open (auto-mip on the monolith, which silently re-passed the whole 8192² every redraw, is gone).

OPTIONAL GPU-INSTANCED PATH (end-state, gated): markers can be rendered via AbstractInstance (Satisfactory's instanced-mesh system) on a hidden marker actor captured by an orthographic USceneCaptureComponent2D per tile region; add/remove become O(1) AddInstance/RemoveInstance and the Z-filter/layer toggles become material params. This is the true zero-CPU-redraw end-state but is gated behind the canvas-tile path landing first.
asyncThreading:
CONVERGENCE MODEL (no cancel/restart thrash): the cancel-on-every-event design is deleted. Ingestion and drawing are fully decoupled. Build/remove hooks do only O(1) work: update Buildings/Grid/Z-index, mark the affected tile(s) dirty, and (on the server) bump the tile snapshot version and enqueue a snapshot rebuild. Drawing is a single long-lived convergent coroutine that drains DirtyTiles forever; it is NEVER cancelled. New dirty tiles arriving mid-pass simply extend the queue (a tile already in the queue is coalesced by its bit), so completed draw work is never discarded. Under a belt-drag the queue absorbs events and converges continuously instead of restarting from scratch and producing zero frames.

FRAME-RELATIVE BUDGET (issue #10): keep FTickTimeBudget (await_ready stays false until a fraction of this tick's frame time is consumed, then resumes next frame) but await at TILE granularity, plus the primitive cap (MaxPrimitivesPerFrame) inside a tile to bound GPU submission. So per frame the rasterizer spends ≤ X% of frame time AND ≤ MaxPrimitivesPerFrame — two independent ceilings, one CPU one GPU. An explicit user-triggered full-redraw button (issue #10) just sets all populated tiles dirty.

OFF-GAME-THREAD WORK: (a) Snapshot serialization/compression (building a tile blob from slim records) runs on a worker task (Async/UE::Tasks), not the game thread; only the final atomic swap of the snapshot pointer + version touches the game thread. (b) Tile bitmap rasterization stays on the render thread (FCanvas/RHI), driven from the budgeted game-thread coroutine. (c) On the server, the InitialBuildableGather O(N²) synchronous stall is replaced by a one-pass O(N) bucketing of engine buildables into grid cells on a worker, then lazy per-tile snapshot generation on first request. (d) Network send/receive of snapshots is handled by ReliableMessaging on its own transport, off the game-critical path. Pre-resolve & pin all distinct icon textures before any draw pass so the loop never co_await AsyncLoadObject mid-rasterization.
networkTransport:
Replace the bespoke RCO slice protocol (3 unchecked TMap::Find null-derefs, int16 slice overflow at ~63 MB, full synchronous per-join serialize, reliable-multicast-per-event) with the in-repo ReliableMessaging plugin (UReliableMessagingSubsystem::SendTaggedMessage / BulkDataReplication), which is purpose-built for reliable large-payload, backpressured, per-player transfer — fixing #9 by construction.

JOIN (streaming, AoI-scoped, not one-shot): the client opens the map -> sends its AoI rect -> server replies with the manifest (tile list + version per tile) for that AoI, then streams each tile snapshot blob via ReliableMessaging (its own framing, acks, and flow control — no hand-rolled int16 counter, no manual FBufferWriter-in-a-TMap). The client renders tiles as they arrive (progressive map fill). Crucially the server NEVER serializes the whole CurrentBuildingData per joiner: it serves immutable, already-built, ref-counted snapshot blobs (TSharedRef<const TArray<uint8>>) shared across all joiners -> join memory O(joiners + AoI) instead of O(joiners·N). Tiles the client never looks at are never sent.

DELTAS (not reliable-multicast-per-event): a build/remove bumps the affected tile's version. The server broadcasts a tiny "tile (x,y) -> vN" version notice (a few bytes, coalesced per net tick). A client holding that tile and currently viewing it requests the new snapshot (or a per-tile delta: added/removed record lists for that tile); a client not viewing it just records the version and lazily re-pulls when it next enters AoI. This collapses the per-event full add/remove-array reliable multicast into a constant-size version ping plus on-demand pull.

BACKPRESSURE & ROBUSTNESS: ReliableMessaging provides the windowed/acked transfer and connection-timeout handling; per-player transfer state is owned by the plugin keyed on a weak PlayerController, with disconnect teardown — eliminating the timeout-races-late-ack null-deref and the per-disconnect buffer/timer leak. A 1-byte protocol version prefixes every blob. Slow clients simply receive tiles slower (windowed), never overflow a reliable channel.

SINGLE-PLAYER: listen host = server+client in one process; the "transport" is a direct in-memory handoff of the shared snapshot pointers (no serialization at all), so SP pays zero network cost and the client reads the server's snapshots directly.
serverClientPartitioning:
Explicit split, designed so the client NEVER recomputes datasets on join or on chunk-load.

COMPUTED ONCE & STORED ON THE SERVER (authoritative): (a) the stable-handle building store (or, on a listen host, just the grid+Z-index over engine arrays); (b) the uniform grid and Z-band index; (c) the per-tile snapshot blobs + monotonic per-tile versions; (d) the ClassDrawTable. These are built once at world-load (O(N) bucketing pass on a worker) and mutated incrementally O(1) per build event. They are PERSISTED in the save via IFGSaveInterface (the snapshot blobs + versions + grid are serialized with the world), so a reload does not re-bucket the whole factory — it loads the cache. Snapshot generation is lazy: a tile's blob is (re)built only when its version is stale AND someone requests it (a viewer or a save flush).

CLIENT (near-stateless consumer): holds ONLY (a) the atlas pages for visible tiles (VRAM, fixed budget), (b) slim records for AoI tiles (so it can re-rasterize on zoom/Z-filter without a server round-trip), (c) the tile-version table for its AoI. On join it pulls AoI snapshots; on map-pan/AoI-change it pulls newly-entered tiles and evicts left tiles; on a build event it gets a version ping and lazily re-pulls. The client computes draw geometry (ComputeDrawGeometry) only for the few buildings in tiles it is actively rasterizing — never for the whole factory, never on join.

ALIGNMENT TO WORLD PARTITION / CHUNK STREAMING: tiles are sized to align with WP cell granularity so "client entered a new WP region" maps directly to "pull these tile snapshots." Chunk-load is O(1): look up tile version, fetch blob if absent — no recompute. Per-tile versioning + dirty invalidation means a far-away edit invalidates only its tile and never touches the client's current view.

EXPLICIT RESOURCE TRADE: we spend server RAM/disk on the tile cache (≈ the slim-record footprint + compressed blobs, tens of MB at 1 M; persisted to disk in the save) and a little server CPU per mutation (rebuild one tile snapshot, O(buildings in tile)) to BUY: client join = O(AoI) not O(N); client chunk-load = O(1) lookup; client CPU/GPU bounded by AoI/atlas; server bandwidth = only viewed tiles + tiny version pings instead of full-dataset reliable multicast.

SINGLE-PLAYER vs DEDICATED: SP (listen host) — server and client are the same process; the client reads the server's snapshot pointers directly (zero serialization, zero copy), and the host iterates engine subsystems per dirty tile so there is effectively ONE copy of the map (the engine's) plus the grid/snapshot cache. DEDICATED — the thin client lacks subsystem data, so it relies entirely on streamed snapshots/slim records for its AoI; the server is the only place the full store/grid/snapshots exist.
memoryModel:
SERVER (authoritative): slim store ≈ 28 B/building + grid (≈ 8–12 B/building amortized across cell arrays) + Z-index (8 B/building) + tile snapshot cache (compressed, ≈ 10–14 B/building) + ClassDrawTable (per-class, negligible). On a LISTEN HOST the slim store can be dropped (iterate engine arrays per dirty tile), leaving grid+Z+snapshots ≈ 26–34 B/building. No second FTransform copy, no precomputed caches, no IndexRedirector (DELETED — the session-long leak is gone: every structure tracks LIVE count via O(1) remove, never lifetime placements).

CLIENT (thin): O(AoI), NOT O(N). VRAM = the fixed atlas budget (default 64 MB pages + ~32 MB mip/overflow reserve ≈ 96 MB) regardless of factory size — replacing the fixed 256 MB monolith and decoupling VRAM from factory size. Client RAM = slim records for AoI tiles (a few thousand buildings in view ≈ tens of KB to a few MB) + the tile-version table. A client viewing a 256 m×256 m chunk of a 1 M-building megabase holds only that chunk's buildings, not 1 M.

LEAK ELIMINATION: the never-compacting IndexRedirector (grew 4 B per lifetime placement, and worse, lengthened the O(N) scan to O(cumulative-adds)) is gone; the grid/store track live count; the atlas evicts pages with a fixed ceiling; ReliableMessaging owns transfer buffers with disconnect teardown (no per-join leak). Resident memory is FLAT across a long build/dismantle session — the #14 "gets worse over ~1 h" signature is structurally removed.

AFTER: fixed atlas budget ≈ 96 MB (64 MB of 512² pages + ~32 MB mip/overflow reserve), independent of factory size; empty tiles cost 0; clears are scissor-sized per page; mips generated lazily per page only when the map is open.

keyRisks: UE 5.3.2 fork API surface: must verify the exact AbstractInstance AddInstance/RemoveInstance handles and that an orthographic USceneCaptureComponent2D + GetViewOwner isolation works under CSS's renderer before committing to the optional GPU-instanced end-state. The canvas-tile path is the safe primary and does not depend on this.

Atlas page eviction thrash: if a player rapidly pans across more tiles than there are pages, page churn could cause re-rasterization stutter. Mitigate with an AoI prefetch ring, LRU eviction, and a configurable atlas size; server-cached snapshots make regeneration cheap.

Tile-boundary correctness: buildings (long belts, foundations) straddling a tile edge must be drawn into every tile they overlap (insert id into all overlapped grid cells, or draw with a small bleed margin and per-tile scissor) so no geometry is clipped at seams. The grid-cell multi-insert must stay consistent on move/remove.

Persistence/versioning in the save (IFGSaveInterface): embedding tile snapshots in the save risks save-format churn and bloat if not compressed/version-gated; need a clean fallback to rebuild snapshots from the engine arrays if the cached blob is a stale schema version.

ReliableMessaging dependency & ordering: the join/delta protocol must correctly handle a build occurring DURING a client's AoI pull (replay via the tile version: if a tile's version advances mid-transfer, the client re-requests that one tile) and must invalidate snapshots on every mutation to avoid serving stale tiles to late joiners.

Single-precision FVector3f position (0.05 cm edge error) and float16 yaw quantization: visually irrelevant for a minimap but must remove any exact-equality position/transform compares that the old identity-by-transform code relied on (identity is now the stable handle, which already fixes the ambiguous-remove bug from the value-quadtree branch).
Z-draw-order regression: dropping the global Z-sort means overlapping icons/foundations must be ordered by the per-tile Z sort at rasterization; verify layering on dense stacked builds.
killerFeature: Every cost is bounded by VISIBLE WORK, never by factory size N. The server computes each 256 m tile's map snapshot exactly once per mutation and persists it; clients stream only the tiles in their area-of-interest and re-pull just the one tile that changed. So join is O(AoI), chunk-load is O(1), a single placement is O(1), and GPU redraw is hard-capped per frame — which simultaneously dissolves all five verified root causes (the O(N²) index, the second factory copy, the 256 MB TDR monolith, the cancel-restart thrash, and the join-crash protocol) with a single coherent tiled, server-authoritative data flow.

name: Tessera — Stable-Handle Incremental Tile Compositor
philosophy: Evolve the immediate-mode CPU canvas correctly instead of replacing it with exotic GPU machinery. Three couplings caused every verified root cause: identity coupled to array position (the redirector + O(N^2)), the Z-filter coupled to storage order (the global Z-sort), and derived draw data baked per-building (the second copy + the caches). Tessera decouples all three: a stable-handle slot store (TSparseArray + generation) is the single source of identity; a uniform spatial hash grid keyed by that handle serves region queries at O(1) mutation; a separate coarse Z-band index serves the height filter; and ALL screen geometry is recomputed at draw time from a per-CLASS table (hundreds of entries, not millions). The image is a persistent tile pyramid that is never fully cleared and never rasterized in one unbounded pass — instead a frame-relative GPU budget drains a dirty-tile queue, so cost per frame is bounded by wall-clock fraction, not by factory size. Convergent, never cancel-restarted. Minimal engine surface: pure UCanvasRenderTarget2D + RHI scissor/clear, no SceneCapture, no Niagara, no engine source changes — maximally robust and moddable on the 5.3.2 fork. Server is authoritative for derived data; clients stream only their area-of-interest and never recompute on join.
summary: Tessera replaces the CurrentBuildingData TArray + IndexRedirector + Z-sorted quadtree triad with a stable-handle store: TSparseArray<FSlimRecord> (24 B/record) where the slot index + a uint16 generation IS the BuildingId, a uniform fixed-grid spatial hash (TArray of cell buckets over the compile-time world bounds) keyed by that handle, and a coarse 1 m Z-band index for the height slider. All screen-space geometry (corners, screen position, size, rotation) is recomputed on demand in the draw loop from a per-CLASS FClassDrawInfo table built once at gather, killing the ~152-192 B/building derived cache and the duplicated corner math. The render target becomes a persistent tile pyramid (256x256 tiles of a configurable 4096^2 base, default; mip pyramid for zoom) that is never fully cleared; a dirty-tile bitset drives incremental recompositing under a HARD frame-relative GPU budget (fraction of frame time, issue #10) that drains over multiple frames, making a single unbounded RHI submission and thus the Windows TDR structurally impossible. The redraw is a convergent debounced accumulator (never cancel-restarted). The server computes the slim dataset and per-tile snapshots ONCE and is authoritative; joining clients pull only their World-Partition-aligned tiles via the ReliableMessaging plugin's tagged large-payload transport with per-tile versioning and delta updates, fixing the #9 join crash by design and eliminating the reliable-multicast-per-event flood. Single-player runs the same store with networking compiled out of the hot path. Net at 1M buildings: heap 360-430 MB to ~26 MB (host can drop to a thin index over engine arrays), VRAM 256 MB to 64 MB, per-event O(N) to O(1) amortized, initial load O(N^2) to O(N), join from a crash to a backpressured O(AoI) stream.
dataModel:
SINGLE SOURCE OF IDENTITY: TSparseArray<FSlimRecord> Store. The sparse-array slot index (uint32) packed with a parallel TArray<uint16> Generation forms a 48-bit BuildingId handle. TSparseArray gives O(1) Add returning a stable slot, O(1) RemoveAt, free-list slot reuse; positions NEVER shift, so the IndexRedirector and its O(N) reindex + monotonic leak are deleted outright. Generation bumps on free => ABA-safe handles for the net/UI paths.

FSlimRecord (24 B, AoS for cache-local draw): uint32 ClassHash; FVector3f Position (12 B single-precision; ~0.05 cm error at 7.5 km edge, irrelevant at 1 cm/px; NetSerialize already drops scale+quat and sends hash+pos+yaw, proving this is the minimal record); float16 Yaw (top-down map needs only yaw); uint8 Type; uint16 ExtraIndex. Splines/wires/beams (the minority) put polyline points in side-tables TArray<FSplineExtra>/<FWireExtra>/<FBeamExtra> indexed by ExtraIndex; normal buildings allocate zero extra data. SoA is unnecessary at 24 B AoS and would fragment the per-record draw; side-tables already give SoA where it matters (extras).

SPATIAL INDEX: uniform hash grid. World bounds are compile-time constants (WEST/EAST/NORTH/SOUTH), so a flat TArray<TArray<uint32>> of GRID_W*GRID_H fixed cells (~64 m cells => ~136x117 ~16 k cells) replaces TQuadTree<int32>. Add = insert BuildingId into each overlapped cell (O(cells covered) ~ O(1)); remove = erase from those cells (cell list cached in a side map or recomputed from Position+class footprint), O(1). No node splitting, no 40 B FBox2D/element, no redirector. Region query visits only overlapping cells: O(result), not O(N).

Z-FILTER decoupled: TMap<int16, TArray<uint32>> ZBands at 1 m resolution (or a sorted TArray<TPair<float,BuildingId>>). The height slider range-selects bands in O(bands+hits). Storage needs NO ordering => the operator<=> Z-sort coupling that forced unstable positions is removed entirely.

PER-CLASS TABLE: TMap<uint32, FClassDrawInfo> built ONCE at gather, sized by classes (hundreds): {Size-after-override, Type, const FCategoryData*, FSplineData*, FWireData*, FBuildLayerData*, extra-rotation, pinned icon}. The draw loop does ONE hash lookup + a few FLOPs (ComputeDrawGeometry) to derive screen pos/corners/size/rotation — the exact FillInCache math, computed at draw time, not stored 1M times.

STORED vs RECOMPUTED vs QUERIED: stored = ClassHash+Position+Yaw+Type+ExtraIndex (non-derivable identity/placement) + grid cell membership + Z-band membership. Recomputed at draw = all screen geometry, corners, the culling AABB. Queried-from-engine on host = nothing per-frame (the slim store is seeded once); the HOST may even drop FSlimRecord entirely and keep only grid+ZBand pointing into AFGBuildableSubsystem / AFGLightweightBuildableSubsystem (engine-as-truth), since those arrays already hold every transform.
renderPipeline:
PERSISTENT TILE PYRAMID, never one unbounded pass. The single 8192^2 (256 MB) target is replaced by a persistent UCanvasRenderTarget2D of configurable base size (default 4096^2 RGBA8 = 64 MB) logically partitioned into 256x256-px tiles (=> 16x16 = 256 tiles at 4096). A small mip chain (built lazily, only for tiles the open map UI samples at the current zoom) provides LOD without storing a separate 8192 surface; mips are generated per-dirty-tile, not whole-texture, so they never silently defeat the scissor.

INCREMENTAL COMPOSITING: a TBitArray<> DirtyTiles (256 bits) + a TSet<FIntPoint> dirty-cell accumulator. Build/remove events mark the overlapped tiles dirty (O(1)) and drain into the store/grid continuously — they NEVER trigger a full redraw. A single persistent compositor coroutine pops dirty tiles and, per tile: RHI ClearRenderTargetView scissored to the tile rect (a free hardware clear of <=256 KB, replacing the 67 M-texel full opaque ClearItem), then re-draws only the buildings whose AABB overlaps that tile (grid query, intersected with the Z-band filter). Because each tile is independent and bounded (256x256 px, a few hundred buildings worst case), a tile is one bounded scissored draw.

GPU COST HARD-BOUNDED: the compositor flushes (EndDrawCanvasToRenderTarget) after either MaxPrimitivesPerFlush (~20 k) OR the frame-relative budget elapses, then co_awaits NextTick and resumes the SAME persistent target WITHOUT re-clearing. One conceptual "redraw" of a megabase becomes ceil(primitives/budget) bounded RHI submissions across many frames => no submission approaches the ~2 s TDR threshold. The map self-heals: a partially-composited frame shows stale tiles until their turn, never a crash.

VRAM CEILING INDEPENDENT OF FACTORY SIZE: 64 MB base + <=~21 MB lazy mips, fixed regardless of 200 k or 1 M buildings (configurable to 2048^2=16 MB on low-VRAM). The global FCanvas::GetBatchedElements hook (process-wide tax + cross-mod static_cast hazard) is deleted: the scissor is applied via the mod's own RHI scissor set around its own tile draws, so no other canvas in the game is rerouted. Icons are pre-resolved and pinned before the canvas opens, so the draw loop never co_awaits AsyncLoadObject mid-pass.
asyncThreading:
CONVERGENT, NEVER CANCEL-RESTARTED. The fatal cancel-on-every-event pattern (RedrawMap->Cancel, re-paying the non-cancellable O(N) ingestion every restart, zero completed frames mid-drag) is replaced by a single long-lived compositor coroutine plus a lock-free producer queue. Build/remove hooks only enqueue (BuildingId, dirty-cell set) — O(1) — and set tiles dirty; they never touch the coroutine. The coroutine loops forever: drain the queue into Store/grid/ZBand (cheap O(1) ops), then while DirtyTiles non-empty, pop and composite tiles until the budget is spent, then yield. Completed tile work is NEVER discarded; a new event during compositing just adds tiles to the still-running drain.

FRAME-RELATIVE BUDGET (issue #10 by design): reuse the existing FTickTimeBudget model but as a fraction of frame time, not absolute ms. Budget = MaxFrameFraction (default 0.25) * (1/TargetFPS); the awaiter samples FPlatformTime::Cycles() and yields to the next GFrameCounter once the fraction is spent. Granularity fixed: await ONCE per tile (or per K buildings), not per primitive — eliminating the ~9*N per-primitive awaiter+Cycles() overhead. The budget adapts: if the last frame ran long, shrink this frame's slice.

OFF-GAME-THREAD WORK: the gather/seed pass (iterate engine arrays -> slim records -> grid/ZBand build) runs as an async task; only the final FCanvas DrawItem emission must be on the game thread (UE canvas constraint), and that is exactly what the budget paces. On a DEDICATED SERVER the entire draw half is compiled out (IsServerOnly early-out before any canvas work) — the server only maintains Store/grid + per-tile snapshot generation, off the critical path. Spline polylines are cached into the slim side-tables at ingest, so the draw loop never dereferences a live USplineComponent (removing the mid-pass stale-actor hazard).
networkTransport:
REPLACE the broken RCO slice protocol (null-deref Find, int16 slice overflow at ~63 MB, per-join full synchronous serialize, move-unsafe FBufferWriter, reliable-multicast-per-event) with the in-repo ReliableMessaging plugin's tagged large-payload transport: SendTaggedMessage(PC, Tag, TArray<uint8>) + RegisterTaggedMessageHandler over its dedicated side-channel net connection (TCP/Steam/EOS). It already chunks, acks, and backpressures large payloads off the gameplay reliable channel, so the int16 overflow and channel-saturation classes vanish by construction.

JOIN = TILE STREAM, NOT ONE-SHOT. The server holds ONE TSharedRef<const FTileSnapshot> per tile (slim records for that tile, ~24 B each, regenerated lazily on a per-tile dirty version counter). A joining client subscribes; the server streams tiles ordered by the client's area-of-interest (spawn/camera tile first, World-Partition-aligned), each message tagged Carto.Tile.<id> carrying {tileId, version, payload}. Backpressure is the plugin's: N in-flight tiles, next sent on ack. No giant up-front serialize, no per-joiner full copy (snapshots are shared-ref, pinned by all joiners => O(N) total server memory, not O(joiners*N)).

DELTA UPDATES, NOT MULTICAST-PER-EVENT: post-join, mutations bump the owning tile's version; the server batches per-tick per-tile deltas {tileId, version, added[], removedIds[]} and sends only to clients whose AoI includes that tile (or who have it cached). A client comparing its cached tile version pulls a fresh snapshot if it fell too far behind (coalesced resync). This eliminates the NetMulticast Reliable flood entirely. A 1-byte protocol version prefixes every payload. Slim records make each transfer 12-15x cheaper: 200 k-building join ~5 MB total (vs ~3.6 MB raw but thousands of RTTs before); windowed tile pull cuts a ~2000-round-trip join to a few hundred.
serverClientPartitioning:
AUTHORITATIVE SERVER, THIN CLIENT — clients NEVER recompute on join or chunk-load. SERVER computes ONCE and STORES: the slim Store (ClassHash+Position+Yaw+Type+Extra), the grid, the ZBand index, the per-class FClassDrawInfo, and per-tile FTileSnapshot byte blobs with version counters. These are the canonical derived dataset. The client receives ready-to-use slim records per tile and feeds them straight into its own local Store+grid+tile compositor — it derives only pixel geometry (cheap, local, GPU-bound), never the dataset.

WORLD-PARTITION ALIGNMENT: tiles map 1:1 onto a coarse spatial partition; as the client's camera/AoI moves (map pan or actual world streaming), it pulls only tiles entering AoI and evicts cold tiles (LRU), so a client browsing one corner of a megabase holds only that corner's records + the composited image, not the whole factory. Per-tile version + delta invalidation means a changed tile invalidates exactly one snapshot, not the world.

PERSISTENCE: per-tile snapshots are a runtime cache keyed by tile version; NOT embedded in the save (the engine save already holds the buildables, and IFGSaveInterface-embedding derived data risks staleness/migration cost). On world load the server rebuilds Store+snapshots in one O(N) async pass; thereafter snapshots are regenerated lazily only for dirtied tiles.

SINGLE-PLAYER / LISTEN HOST = server+client in one process: the SAME Store serves both; the network layer is bypassed (local AoI reads the local Store directly, no serialize). The host may run engine-as-truth (drop FSlimRecord, point grid/ZBand at AFGBuildableSubsystem/AFGLightweightBuildableSubsystem) for ~zero second-copy. DEDICATED SERVER (thin, no GPU): builds Store+grid+snapshots, runs NO compositor/canvas (IsServerOnly early-out), streams to clients. DEDICATED CLIENT (lacks subsystem data): keeps the slim Store fed by the tile stream — this is the only configuration that holds a per-client record copy, and only for its AoI tiles.

TRADE: server spends CPU once (O(N) gather) + RAM (~26 MB slim Store + ~bounded snapshot cache @1M) + disk none (runtime cache) + bandwidth O(AoI) per client; in exchange every client avoids all dataset recompute, joins are bounded and crash-free, and chunk-load pulls are incremental.
memoryModel:
PER-RECORD: 24 B FSlimRecord (vs 344-432 B FBuildingData) — 14-18x. Derived cache (FNormalDataCache/FRectangleDataCache/VisualBoxCache ~152-192 B) ELIMINATED (recomputed at draw). IndexRedirector (4 B/lifetime-placement, unbounded leak) DELETED. Quadtree 40 B FBox2D/element DELETED, replaced by grid: ~4 B per (building,cell) membership, ~1.5 cells/building avg => ~6 B/building. ZBand: ~6 B/building. Generation: 2 B/slot. Per-class table: O(classes) ~ tens of KB total. Net resident per building ~24+6+6+2 = ~38 B client-side; host with engine-as-truth ~12 B (grid+ZBand only).

VRAM: persistent tile target 4096^2 RGBA8 = 64 MB (config 2048=16 MB / 8192=256 MB) + lazy mips <=~21 MB, FIXED regardless of factory size. No second 256 MB clear surface; clears are scissored HW clears.

NO TRANSIENT DOUBLING: gather iterates engine arrays by const-ref (the by-value 'Intentional copies' deep copy is removed); join snapshots are shared-ref pinned, not per-joiner copies. NetSerialize emits only Size bytes (the 2 KB/slice stack-tail leak gone). Slot reuse + generation keeps the store compact across churn — resident memory is FLAT under the #14 build/dismantle repro, the key success criterion.

keyRisks: Generation-tagged TSparseArray handles: any path that keys a BuildingId across remove+add (RCO/UI) must validate generation or it reads a recycled slot. Mitigation: 48-bit handle = slot:32 + gen:16, checked on every external deref.

ComputeDrawGeometry must reproduce FillInCache math pixel-identically or icons/rectangles shift. Mitigation: extract one shared pure helper used by both old and new paths during transition, diff-render a large save, then delete stored fields. Single-precision FVector3f forbids any exact-equality position compare (identity is now the handle anyway).

Persistent target + scissored clear: the 2nd BeginDraw must NOT implicitly clear the RT, and a cancel mid-tile leaves a stale tile until next pass (self-heals). Must verify UE 5.3.2 BeginDrawCanvasToRenderTarget preserves contents and that RHI scissored ClearRenderTargetView is reachable from the mod without engine changes.

Grid cell size tuning: long belts / huge foundations span many cells (insert cost) vs large cells inflate region-query overdraw. Mitigation: ~64 m default, expose as config; oversized buildables can fall back to a coarse overflow list.

ReliableMessaging plugin is the load-bearing transport — must confirm it ships/links in the dedicated-server + Steam/EOS shipping configs the mod targets, and that its connection-establishment handshake completes before first tile send.
